verses.1: And the young man, Shmuel, served Jehovah before His face. The words of Jehovah were precious in those days; no one could predict them.
verses.2: And on that day, he lay there in his place, and his eyes began to swell so much that he could no longer see.
verses.3: And God will be raised before He dies, and Shmuel will lie in the house of Jehovah, where God resides.
verses.4: And Jehovah called to Shmulai, and he said, “Here I am.”
verses.5: And he ran to Eliezer. He said, “I am here because you called for me.” But Eliezer replied, “I did not call for you again. Go away and lie down.” Then he went away and lay down.
verses.6: And Jehovah continued to call upon Shmulai. Shmulai rose up and went to Eleyi. He said, “I am here because you have called me.” But Eleyi replied, “No, son, do not come back.”
verses.7: And Shmu’el did not know Jehovah before, nor could he understand the words of Jehovah.
verses.8: And Jehovah gathered up His name in the threefold manner. He arose and went to Eli. He said, “I am here, for you have called me.” Then He created Eli, because Jehovah had called the young man.
verses.9: And He said to Samuel, “Go and lie down. If He calls you, then you shall say, ‘The words of the LORD are true.’ Then Samuel will go and lie down in his place.”
verses.10: And Jehovah came and stood there, calling out His name over and over again. Then He said, “Shamuel, speak!” For He heard Your servant.
verses.11: And the LORD said to Samuel, “Behold, I will do a miracle among the Israelites. Everyone who hears about it will be filled with joy.”
verses.12: On that day, I will bring to life everything I have said in his house.
verses.13: And I told him that I would judge his house forever, because he knew that his sons were being slandered, and he did nothing to stop them.
verses.14: And therefore, I will bless the house of Eli forever. May the evils that befell the house of Eli be turned into blessings through sacrifices and offerings, forever.
verses.15: And Shemuel lay down until morning. Then he opened the doors of the Temple of Jehovah. Shemuel was afraid of what might be seen from above.
verses.16: And he called out to me his name, Shemuel. Shemuel said, “Son, come here.”
verses.17: And he said, “What is this thing that I have spoken to you? Please do not be discouraged by it. This is what God will do for you. And if you become discouraged by it, then all the things that I have spoken to you will be in vain.”
verses.18: And Shemuel told him all these things. He didn’t leave out any details. And God said, “This is what is good in His eyes; let him do it.”
verses.19: And Shemuel grew up, and Yahweh was with him. He did not abandon him in any of his endeavors.
verses.20: And all of Israel knew from Dan to Be’er Sheva that the Lord had indeed spoken through the prophet Elijah.
verses.21: And Jehovah became visible in His glory, just as Jehovah revealed Himself to Israel through His words.
